previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fatigue, somnolence, and rigors in the setting of relapsed refractory multiple myeloma. He was found to have coagulase-negative staph bacteremia, likely originating from his port, though no clear source was identified. He was treated with a week of IV vancomycin and will complete a 14-day course at home with nursing support. During admission, he developed transient groin pain, which resolved without intervention, and a new systolic murmur attributed to anemia, with echocardiogram ruling out endocarditis. Altered mental status was linked to hypoglycemia and opioid use; insulin regimen was adjusted with endocrinology input. A small subgaleal hematoma was incidentally noted on head CT with no clinical significance. He received one unit of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia and was discharged in stable condition with plans to resume chemotherapy after antibiotic completion.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT abdomen and pelvis

INDICATION:  ___ man with a history of multiple myeloma, who had
chemotherapy yesterday and now presents with LLQ and inguinal abdominal pain. 
Evaluate for etiology of left lower quadrant and left inguinal pain.  NO_PO
contrast.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT images of the abdomen and pelvis were acquired
without intravenous contrast. Non-contrast scan has several limitations in
detecting vascular and parenchymal organ abnormalities, including tumor
detection.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 5.0 s, 54.5 cm; CTDIvol = 16.8 mGy (Body) DLP = 914.3
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 914 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis exams dated ___ and ___.
CT chest dated ___.
MRI abdomen and pelvis dated ___.
Scrotal ultrasound dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Detailed evaluation of the solid organs, soft tissues, and vessels is limited
without the use of intravenous contrast. Within this limitation:

LOWER CHEST: Bibasilar atelectasis in the partially imaged lower lungs is mild
and similar to the prior exam.  No evidence of a pleural effusion or
pericardial effusion.  Hypoattenuation of the cardiac blood pool again
indicates anemia.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogeneous attenuation throughout.  No
evidence of focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced scan.  No
evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder
is within normal limits.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced scan.  No pancreatic
ductal dilatation.  No peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size.  No evidence of focal
renal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced scan.  Smaller lesions
consistent with cysts in the right kidney were better evaluated on the prior
MR. ___ calcifications in the right lower lobe are unchanged and likely
nonobstructing stones (series 601b, image 43).  No hydronephrosis or
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber and wall thickness throughout.  Colonic diverticulosis is
moderate.  The rectum is within normal limits.  The appendix is normal.  No
bowel obstruction, free air, intra-abdominal fluid collection, or pneumatosis.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder is partially distended with persistent mass effect
from the adjacent soft tissue mass in the left hemipelvis.  The urinary
bladder is otherwise unremarkable.  The distal ureters are unremarkable.  No
free fluid in the pelvis.  A 3.9 x 5.8 x 3.3-cm lobulated soft tissue mass in
the left hemipelvis, previously measured 3.8 x 6 x 3.5 cm, unchanged and
biopsied with a plasma cell dyscrasia on pathology from ___ (series 2,
image 74; series 601b, image 45).

The patient has had prior radical prostatectomy with surgical clips in the
pelvis unchanged.

LYMPH NODES: No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  No pelvic or
inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: No abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease is
noted.

BONES:  T12 superior endplate deformities is unchanged since at least ___ (series 602b, image 49).  No evidence of an acute fracture or new lytic
or sclerotic lesions.  Old left posterior rib fractures are unchanged.  Right
convex curvature of the lumbar spine is mild, unchanged.

SOFT TISSUES: A moderate fat-containing right inguinal hernia is unchanged
(Series 2, image 82).  Soft tissue stranding in the left inguinal canal
persists and is slightly more pronounced since ___ but similar in
appearance to ___ (series 2, image 78, 79).

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of an acute intra-abdominal or pelvic process.
2. Nonspecific soft tissue stranding in the left inguinal region  overall
unchanged from ___ and was evaluated with ultrasound on ___.
3. No significant interval change in the known left perivesicular pelvic mass,
previously biopsied with pathology "involved by plasma cell dyscrasia."
4. Colonic diverticulosis.
5. Non-obstructing right lower pole renal stones, unchanged.
